analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 11.5.26
key_insights: Futures mixed pre-market (Nasdaq -80bps, S&P +10bps, RTY +25bps) as markets price in midterm election results. The GS desk saw heavy rotational flow on 11/4: broad buying of hyperscalers (installed compute) against broad supply in tech names that sell into, power, or build out datacenters.
Overnight price action points to more rotation: semis -3% versus AMZN/GOOGL/META/AAPL +1% in the pre-market. SMH -2% and DRAM -4% remain under pressure.
Biggest idiosyncratic pre-market moves: U +23%, APP +20%, QCOM -10%, ZG -15%, SNAP -10%, HUBS -9%, EXPE -6%, ARM -5%.

QCOM revenue of $10.3bn was in line with GS ($10.2bn Street). Gross margin of 52.4% was below GS (53.5%) and the Street (53.3%). Operating EPS of $2.17 was in line. FY1Q EPS guide ex-SBC of $2.25 is below GS ($2.41) and the Street ($2.33), while revenue guide of $10.8bn is above the Street ($10.5bn).

QCOM datacenter: three multi-generation custom silicon engagements with hyperscalers (up from two) are entering wafer production. Revenue starts in FY1Q (December) with over $650mn expected, ramping to a ~$7bn exit run rate and $5bn of total datacenter revenue in FY27.

APP beat on Q3 revenue and guided Q4 above prior expectations. It announced a $3.2B buyback, with ~$1.3bn repurchased in Q3 and ~$2.8bn YTD. Negatives: non-GAAP expenses grew QoQ on datacenter hosting and customer acquisition investment, and the Q4 revenue guide implies a modest sequential deceleration.

U (first take): 3Q Vector revenue +40% q/q and +126% y/y. Adj EBITDA of $256.6M beat consensus of $188.9M by ~35%. 4Q guide: revenue $683-691mn vs consensus $601mn, EBITDA $290-295mn vs consensus $201mn.

ARM revenue of $1.44bn beat GS ($1.39bn) and the Street ($1.38bn), but royalty revenue of $670mn missed GS ($707mn) and the Street ($708mn). Licensing revenue of $773mn was well above GS ($677mn). Management said confidence in up to $2bn of AGI CPU revenue across FY27-FY28 has increased over the past 90 days, with first commercial deliveries on track for FY4Q27.

ZG 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of $182mn missed GSe/consensus of $193mn/$192mn on revenue of $724mn against $759mn/$753mn. 4Q26 guide of revenue $635-665mn and EBITDA $100-135mn is below consensus of $708mn and $185mn, and embeds a 10-15% contraction in industry purchase originations.
SNAP 3Q26 ad revenue growth slowed to low-to-mid single digits on brand advertising headwinds, mainly CPG. Subscription revenue grew +84% y/y to ~20% of revenue, with ~30mm paid subscribers.

HUBS 3Q revenue came in ahead but billings growth slowed and 4Q revenue was guided light. EXPE 3Q gross bookings, revenue and adj EBITDA beat the Street, but 4Q guidance was below as growth is expected to moderate on softer demand.
Amazon is adding Uber Eats delivery perks for Prime members, with the Uber delivery fee waived on orders of $25 or more, a week after DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart (per Bloomberg).

Micron has halted construction of its $4.5bn Taoyuan, Taiwan plant over a labor dispute, per Bloomberg. Apple is cutting internal AI spending caps for engineers to $200/day from $300, with possible cuts to $100 (per Bloomberg).
Google plans to invest US$15bn in Malaysian data centers over 2027-2028. GS Japan hardware analysts see potential order benefits for Mitsubishi Electric, Fuji Electric, Fujikura, Daihen and Hitachi.

Asia closed mixed: Hang Seng +3.6%, Nikkei -1.79%, Kospi -5.28%, with Hynix -9%, Samsung -7.5% and Tokyo Electron -9%. Europe is up about 80bps, helped by financials and healthcare, which have low AI exposure.

Street rating changes: ARM downgraded to Neutral by President Capital Management, CSCO to Equal-Weight by Morgan Stanley, HUBS to Underweight by Cantor and to Equal-Weight by Morgan Stanley, SWKS to Equal-Weight by Barclays. CNK was upgraded to Overweight by Morgan Stanley.

sector_views.rationale: The desk saw rotation out of semis and datacenter build-out suppliers and into hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, AAPL).

earnings_insights: QCOM FQ4 (reported 11/4 after the close): revenue $10.3bn reported vs GS $10.2bn and Street $10.2bn. Gross margin 52.4% vs GS 53.5% and Street 53.3%. Operating EPS $2.17 vs GS $2.16 and Street $2.17. FY1Q guide: revenue $10.8bn vs Street $10.5bn, EPS ex-SBC $2.25 vs GS $2.41 and Street $2.33.
QCOM segments: QCT revenue $9.02bn vs $8.78bn GS/Street. Handsets $5.1bn vs $5.2bn. Automotive $1.99bn vs $1.7bn. IoT $1.89bn vs $1.8bn.

ARM FQ2 (reported 11/4 after the close): revenue $1.44bn vs GS $1.39bn and Street (VA) $1.38bn. Operating EPS $0.52 vs $0.48. Operating margin 44.2% vs GS 42.2%. Royalty $670mn vs GS $707mn and Street $708mn. Licensing $773mn vs GS $677mn. FY3Q guide: revenue $1.54bn midpoint vs Street $1.52bn, operating EPS $0.56 vs Street $0.55.

U 3Q (reported, call at 8:30am ET on 11/5): Vector revenue +40% q/q and +126% y/y. Adj EBITDA $256.6M vs consensus $188.9M. 4Q guide: revenue $683-691mn vs consensus $601mn, EBITDA $290-295mn vs consensus $201mn.

ZG 3Q26 (reported): adjusted EBITDA $182mn vs GSe $193mn and Visible Alpha consensus $192mn. Revenue $724mn vs $759mn GSe and $753mn consensus. For Sale revenue flat y/y at $489mn, Rentals +26% y/y to $220mn. 4Q26 guide: revenue $635-665mn vs consensus $708mn, adjusted EBITDA $100-135mn vs consensus $185mn.
TKO 3Q26 (reported): WWE revenue/adj EBITDA $399M/$217M vs Visible Alpha consensus $413M/$225M. UFC $519M/$285M vs consensus $491M/$303M. Management raised 2026 guidance.
APP Q3 (reported): beat versus GSe and Visible Alpha Street estimates on revenue and adj EBITDA. Q3 buybacks ~$1.3bn, ~$2.8bn YTD, new $3.2B buyback announced.
EXPE Q3'26 (reported): gross bookings, revenue and adj EBITDA exceeded the Street and guidance. 4Q gross bookings guide was below expectations. B2B partners now ~75k, direct traffic ~2/3 of bookings.

SNAP Q3'26 (reported): total revenue growth in the mid-teens % y/y, in line with expectations. Advertising growth slowed to low-to-mid single digits. Other (subscription) revenue +84% y/y at ~20% of total revenue.

Pre-open earnings on 11/5: AAP, APD, BDX, CAH, CI, CMI, COP, DUK, KMB, PH, RL, SO, SRE, USFD. Post-close: AKAM, DVN, ED, LYV, MCHP, SPG, WYNN (and ABNB, AFRM, AXON, DKNG, NET, LYFT, TEAM, among others).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Yield lower in the pre-market, a level reading rather than an official print.
Crude up after the prior day's rally, while the desk cites a more likely near-term Iran resolution.
The prior payrolls print the market compares against when the report is released on Friday 11/6.

risk_factors: Rotation out of semis and datacenter suppliers could continue (SMH -2%, DRAM -4%, Kospi -5.28%).
Housing weakness: ZG guides to a 10-15% contraction in industry purchase originations, with higher mortgage rates hitting mortgage revenue.
Brand advertising weakness (CPG) is slowing SNAP's ad growth. Softer travel demand is cited in EXPE's 4Q guide.
Micron's Taiwan plant halt and possible reversal of a local labor agreement threaten memory supply buildout.
QCOM margin headwinds and a tepid smartphone market.
vol_and_positioning: The desk described the midterm elections as a clearing event, citing strong historical post-midterm performance (especially with gridlock) and clean positioning.
Heavy rotational flow on 11/4: broad buying of hyperscalers against broad selling of semis and datacenter build-out suppliers. The desk did not see chasing in consumer or financials.
geopolitical: The desk cites a more likely near-term Iran resolution as one reason for the prior day's rally.
Google's US$15bn Malaysia data center investment, with Asian data center construction booming faster than the US, where opposition movements are slowing projects.
Micron halted construction of a Taiwan plant over a labor dispute.
